approachQuestion.prompt:
Affordable Inspection Runs

An array `fees` lists the cost of inspecting consecutive stations. Return the NUMBER of non-empty contiguous segments with total fee at most `cap`. Count segments with different start or end indices separately, even when their values are identical.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ fees[i] ≤ 1000000; 0 ≤ cap ≤ 10^12.
• All sums and the answer fit in signed 64-bit integers. Stations remain in their original order.

Examples:
1. fees = [1,0,2], cap = 2 → 5. The only rejected segment is the full array.
2. fees = [0,0,0], cap = 0 → 6.
3. fees = [], cap = 3 → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: All sums and the answer fit in signed 64-bit integers. Stations remain in their original order.

options.text: Maintain a sum and a left boundary. For each new right endpoint, remove leftmost fees while the sum exceeds cap. Add right - left + 1 to the answer.
options.feedback: Non-negative fees imply that exactly the starts from left through right are valid for this endpoint. If the window is empty, the contribution is zero.

options.text: Use the same boundary repair, store the resulting left boundary for every right endpoint in an array, then sum right - left[right] + 1.
options.feedback: This counts every valid segment correctly, but the array can be replaced by adding each contribution immediately.

options.text: Maintain a valid window and add one to the answer whenever its non-empty sum is within cap.
options.feedback: For fees [0,0] and cap 0 this counts two endpoints, but there are three valid segments: both singletons and their pair.

options.text: For each endpoint count only starts whose segment sum equals cap.
options.feedback: The condition includes sums below cap. With fees [1] and cap 2 the correct count is one, while no segment has sum exactly two.

feedback.reason: For a fixed right endpoint, every start from left through right forms a valid suffix: exactly right-left+1 segments.
details: Extend right, add its fee, and remove leftmost values until the sum is at most cap. Add right - left + 1 to a running total, without storing individual segments or boundary histories.

For a fixed right endpoint, every start from left through right forms a valid suffix: exactly right-left+1 segments. Counting just one window per endpoint misses those alternatives. Nonnegative fees justify rejecting all earlier starts.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Count valid starts at each endpoint” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two monotone boundaries count all valid starts without storing segments.
details: For each endpoint the repaired window has the earliest valid start. All its suffixes are valid, and every earlier start is invalid. Each boundary advances at most n times in total; only sum, boundaries, and count are retained.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Overlapping starts share one sum and monotone boundaries; this method does not restart a scan from every start.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Only left, right, sum, and total count remain; no list of valid segments is stored.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each boundary crosses the fee array once. No sorting or logarithmic lookup occurs.
